```{r packages}
# ── analysis settings ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

hist_end   <- 2010L
fut_start  <- 2035L
fut_end    <- 2065L
spei_scale <- 12L
spei_inf_cap <- 4
water_year <- TRUE
hindcast <- TRUE

output_dir <- "data/rapid/outputs"
input_dir  <- "data/rapid/inputs"

exposure_path <- list.files(

monthly_drought_path <- file.path(

)

  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +

      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size + 1),

    )
}

# ── SPEI classification thresholds ───────────────────────────────────────────

spei_labels  <- c("Extreme drought", "Severe drought", "Moderate drought",

                  "Moderately wet", "Very wet", "Extremely wet")
spei_colours <- c("#7F1D1D", "#DC2626", "#F97316",
```

---

# Overview

## What is the Drought Exposure Indicator?

The **Drought Exposure** indicator measures how much projected climate change is expected to
shift long-term drought conditions at each NPS water supply. Drought is characterized using the
**Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI)**, a widely used metric that
accounts for both precipitation and atmospheric evaporative demand (potential evapotranspiration, PET).

The indicator reports the **change in mean 12-month SPEI** between the historical baseline period
and the future projection window across a full ensemble of LOCA2 climate models and SSPs.

$$\Delta\text{SPEI} = \overline{\text{SPEI}}^{(\text{future})} - \overline{\text{SPEI}}^{(\text{historical})}$$

**Negative Δ SPEI → drying (worsening drought exposure)**  
**Positive Δ SPEI → wetting (improving conditions)**

Therefore, a *more negative* value is *worse*, so `add_standardized_indicators()` is called with `invert = TRUE`.

## Why 12-Month SPEI?

SPEI can be calculated at different accumulation scales (1, 3, 6, 12 months). A 12-month
accumulation (`spei_scale = 12`) captures long-term hydrological drought. It is less 
sensitive to individual wet or dry months and more indicative of sustained multi-season stress.

## Infinite SPEI Values

SPEI is derived by fitting a log-logistic distribution to the calibration-period
water balance, then transforming probabilities through the standard normal quantile
function. When a future month's accumulated balance falls **below the calibration
minimum**, the fitted distribution assigns it a probability of zero — and the normal
quantile of zero is **−Inf**. This is not a data error; it signals that projected
conditions would be historically unprecedented. The symmetric +Inf case exists but
is rare here.

Before computing mean SPEI, I capped the raw Inf values with ±`r spei_inf_cap`.
This keeps them influential without making averages numerically meaningless. The
original counts are retained in the `raw_spei_*_inf_months` diagnostic columns;
`raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months` is the most useful — it records how
often future reporting months hit −Inf before capping them, which indicates the 
reported change in SPEI is a "conservative" lower bound on drying severity.
**Why SPEI-12 reduces infinite values:** Summing twelve months of water balance
produces a wider, more continuously distributed series than any single month or
season. Arid-climate months with identical near-zero balances — which concentrate
probability mass at the distribution boundary and make −Inf easy to trigger — are
averaged away. I first attempted to do SPEI-6, but it produced MANY Inf values.
SPEI-12 retains fewer infinite values than SPEI-3 or SPEI-6 across this water supply 
network while still capturing the multi-season drought signal relevant to
reservoir storage and groundwater recharge.

## SPEI Classification

```{r spei-ref-table, echo=FALSE}
tibble(
  `SPEI value` = c("< −2.0", "−2.0 to −1.5", "−1.5 to −1.0",
                   "−1.0 to +1.0",
                   "+1.0 to +1.5", "+1.5 to +2.0", "> +2.0"),
  Category = spei_labels,
  Interpretation = c("Exceptional water deficit; severe operational risk",
                     "Serious multi-season water deficit",
                     "Noticeable deficit; may stress smaller supplies",
                     "Conditions within historical normal range",
                     "Above-average moisture; favorable conditions",
                     "Significant surplus",
                     "Record wetness")) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "SPEI drought classification thresholds")
```

```{r load-results}
exposure <- read_csv(exposure_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

exposure %>%
  summarize(
    n_water_supplies = n(),
    n_parks = n_distinct(park_unit),
    pct_drying_p50 = mean(raw_spei_change_p50 < 0,  na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    pct_wetting_p50 = mean(raw_spei_change_p50 > 0,  na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    mean_delta_spei_p50 = mean(raw_spei_change_p50, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_delta_spei_p50 = median(raw_spei_change_p50, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_pct_models_drying = mean(raw_spei_models_showing_decrease, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_p10_p90_spread = mean(raw_spei_change_p90 - raw_spei_change_p10, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_model_count = median(raw_spei_model_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_future_report_pct_neg_inf = if ("raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months" %in% names(exposure)) {
      mean(raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value") %>%
  mutate(Value = round(Value, 3)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = glue::glue("Summary statistics for the Drought Exposure indicator ({basename(exposure_path)})"))
```

# SPEI Fit Diagnostics

The updated exposure function caps infinite SPEI values before computing mean SPEI change:

- `-Inf` becomes `-spei_inf_cap`.
- `Inf` becomes `spei_inf_cap`.
- `NaN` remains `NA`.

The final exposure output also retains diagnostic fields for total and reporting-window infinite values.
The most drought-relevant diagnostic is `raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months`, which records
how often future reporting months hit `-Inf` before capping.

```{r inf-diagnostic-summary}
inf_required <- c(
  "raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months",
  "raw_spei_models_with_future_report_neg_inf"
)

if (all(inf_required %in% names(exposure))) {

  exposure %>%
    summarise(
      `Mean % extreme dry months` =
        mean(raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months, na.rm = TRUE),
      `Median % extreme dry months` =
        median(raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months, na.rm = TRUE),
      `90th percentile % extreme dry months` =
        quantile(raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
      `Max % extreme dry months` =
        max(raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months, na.rm = TRUE),

      `Mean % affected models` =
        mean(raw_spei_models_with_future_report_neg_inf, na.rm = TRUE),
      `Median % affected models` =
        median(raw_spei_models_with_future_report_neg_inf, na.rm = TRUE),
      `90th percentile % affected models` =
        quantile(raw_spei_models_with_future_report_neg_inf, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
      `Max % affected models` =
        max(raw_spei_models_with_future_report_neg_inf, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      everything(),
      names_to = "Diagnostic",
      values_to = "Percent"
    ) %>%
    mutate(Percent = round(Percent, 3)) %>%
    knitr::kable(
      caption = "Extreme dry SPEI diagnostics across water supplies"
    )

} else {
  tibble(
    Note = "Extreme dry SPEI diagnostic columns were not found."
  ) %>%
    knitr::kable()
}
```

```{r fig-inf-diagnostics, fig.height=5}
if ("raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months" %in% names(exposure)) {
  exposure %>%
    filter(!is.na(raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = col_dry, color = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
    labs(
      title = "Future Reporting Months with Unbounded Dry SPEI Before Capping",
      subtitle = "Higher values indicate months where SPEI hit -Inf before being capped for the mean-change calculation.",
      x = "% of future reporting months with raw SPEI = -Inf",
      y = "Count of water supplies"
    ) +
    theme_rapid()
}
```

# SPEI Time Series — Example Parks

Reconstructing the SPEI time series for selected parks lets us visualise both the historical
calibration period and the projected future trajectory across the full model ensemble.

```{r select-example-parks}
set.seed(42)

quartile_parks <- exposure %>%
  group_by(park_unit) %>%
  slice_min(wsd_source_id, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(quartile = ntile(raw_spei_change_p50, 4)) %>%
  group_by(quartile) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(raw_spei_change_p50)

example_parks <- quartile_parks$park_unit
example_wsd <- quartile_parks$wsd_source_id

quartile_parks %>%
  select(
    park_unit,
    wsd_source_id,
    quartile,
    raw_spei_change_p10,
    raw_spei_change_p50,
    raw_spei_change_p90,
    raw_spei_models_showing_decrease,
    raw_spei_model_count,
    any_of(c("raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months",
             "raw_spei_models_with_future_report_neg_inf"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Example parks — one per quartile of median Δ SPEI")
```

```{r load-monthly-data, cache = TRUE, results = "hide"}
required_monthly_cols <- c(
  "wsd_source_id", "park_unit", "ym", "year", "month", "analysis_year",
  "drought_period", "model", "ssp", "run",
  "monthly_precipitation", "monthly_pet", "climatic_water_balance",
  "source_type", "source_priority", "input_window", "reporting_period"
)

monthly_ds <- arrow::open_dataset(monthly_drought_path)
monthly_cols <- names(monthly_ds)
missing_monthly_cols <- setdiff(required_monthly_cols, monthly_cols)

if (length(missing_monthly_cols) > 0L) {
  stop("Monthly drought file is missing required columns: ", paste(missing_monthly_cols, collapse = ", "))
}

climate_monthly <- monthly_ds %>%
  select(all_of(required_monthly_cols)) %>%
  filter(wsd_source_id %in% example_wsd) %>%
  collect() %>%
  as.data.table()

climate_monthly[, ym := as.IDate(ym)]
climate_monthly[, monthly_balance := climatic_water_balance]
climate_monthly[!is.finite(monthly_balance), monthly_balance := NA_real_]
```

```{r compute-spei-timeseries, cache=TRUE}
# Compute SPEI-12 per model × SSP × water supply using the already assembled
# drought_period rows produced by process_drought_data().

if (water_year) {
  hist_report_start_month <- as.IDate(paste0(hist_start - 1L, "-10-01"))
  hist_report_end_month   <- as.IDate(paste0(hist_end, "-09-01"))
  fut_report_start_month  <- as.IDate(paste0(fut_start - 1L, "-10-01"))
  fut_report_end_month    <- as.IDate(paste0(fut_end, "-09-01"))
} else {
  hist_report_start_month <- as.IDate(paste0(hist_start, "-01-01"))
  hist_report_end_month   <- as.IDate(paste0(hist_end, "-12-01"))
  fut_report_start_month  <- as.IDate(paste0(fut_start, "-01-01"))
  fut_report_end_month    <- as.IDate(paste0(fut_end, "-12-01"))
}

pad_months <- spei_scale - 1L
hist_input_start_month <- seq(hist_report_start_month, by = "-1 month", length.out = pad_months + 1L)[pad_months + 1L]
hist_input_end_month <- hist_report_end_month
fut_input_start_month <- seq(fut_report_start_month, by = "-1 month", length.out = pad_months + 1L)[pad_months + 1L]
fut_input_end_month <- fut_report_end_month

future_ssps <- climate_monthly[
  drought_period == "future",
  unique(.SD),
  .SDcols = c("model", "ssp", "run")
]

cap_spei <- function(x, cap = spei_inf_cap) {
  x[x == Inf] <- cap
  x[x == -Inf] <- -cap
  x[is.nan(x)] <- NA_real_
  x
}

run_spei_values <- function(series_dt, date_col, ref_idx) {
  if (!nrow(series_dt) || !any(ref_idx & !is.na(series_dt$monthly_balance))) {
    return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(series_dt)))
  }

  date_vals <- series_dt[[date_col]]
  ref_dates <- date_vals[ref_idx & !is.na(series_dt$monthly_balance)]

  balance_ts <- ts(
    series_dt$monthly_balance,
    start = c(year(min(date_vals)), month(min(date_vals))),
    frequency = 12
  )

  out <- tryCatch(
    as.numeric(
      SPEI::spei(
        balance_ts,
        scale = spei_scale,
        ref.start = c(year(min(ref_dates)), month(min(ref_dates))),
        ref.end = c(year(max(ref_dates)), month(max(ref_dates))),
        na.rm = TRUE,
        verbose = FALSE
      )$fitted
    ),
    error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, nrow(series_dt))
  )

  cap_spei(out)
}

run_spei_for_park <- function(wsd_id, park, model_id, ssp_id, run_id) {

  hist_data <- climate_monthly[
    wsd_source_id == wsd_id &
      park_unit == park &
      model == model_id &
      ssp == ssp_id &
      run == run_id &
      drought_period == "historical" &
      ym >= hist_input_start_month &
      ym <= hist_input_end_month
  ]

  fut_data <- climate_monthly[
    wsd_source_id == wsd_id &
      park_unit == park &
      model == model_id &
      ssp == ssp_id &
      run == run_id &
      drought_period == "future" &
      ym >= fut_input_start_month &
      ym <= fut_input_end_month
  ]

  setorder(hist_data, ym)
  setorder(fut_data, ym)

  if (nrow(hist_data) < spei_scale || nrow(fut_data) < spei_scale) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  hist_full <- data.table(ym = seq(hist_input_start_month, hist_input_end_month, by = "month"))
  hist_full <- merge(
    hist_full,
    hist_data[, .(ym, monthly_balance)],
    by = "ym",
    all.x = TRUE,
    sort = TRUE
  )

  hist_idx <- hist_full$ym >= hist_report_start_month & hist_full$ym <= hist_report_end_month
  hist_spei <- run_spei_values(hist_full, "ym", hist_idx)

  fut_full <- data.table(ym = seq(fut_input_start_month, fut_input_end_month, by = "month"))
  fut_full <- merge(
    fut_full,
    fut_data[, .(ym, monthly_balance)],
    by = "ym",
    all.x = TRUE,
    sort = TRUE
  )

  future_fit <- rbindlist(
    list(
      hist_full[, .(original_ym = ym, period = "historical", monthly_balance = monthly_balance)],
      fut_full[, .(original_ym = ym, period = "future", monthly_balance = monthly_balance)]
    ),
    use.names = TRUE
  )

  future_fit[, spei_ym := seq(from = hist_input_start_month, by = "month", length.out = .N)]

  future_ref_idx <- future_fit$period == "historical" &
    future_fit$original_ym >= hist_report_start_month &
    future_fit$original_ym <= hist_report_end_month

  future_idx <- future_fit$period == "future" &
    future_fit$original_ym >= fut_report_start_month &
    future_fit$original_ym <= fut_report_end_month

  future_spei <- run_spei_values(future_fit, "spei_ym", future_ref_idx)

  hist_out <- hist_full[hist_idx, .(
    wsd_source_id = wsd_id,
    park_unit = park,
    ym,
    year = year(ym),
    month = month(ym),
    analysis_year = if (water_year) year(ym) + fifelse(month(ym) >= 10, 1L, 0L) else year(ym),
    model = model_id,
    ssp = ssp_id,
    run = run_id,
    period = "historical",
    spei = hist_spei[hist_idx]
  )]

  fut_out <- future_fit[future_idx, .(
    wsd_source_id = wsd_id,
    park_unit = park,
    ym = original_ym,
    year = year(original_ym),
    month = month(original_ym),
    analysis_year = if (water_year) year(original_ym) + fifelse(month(original_ym) >= 10, 1L, 0L) else year(original_ym),
    model = model_id,
    ssp = ssp_id,
    run = run_id,
    period = "future",
    spei = future_spei[future_idx]
  )]

  rbindlist(list(hist_out, fut_out), use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE)[!is.na(spei)]
}

spei_ts_list <- vector("list", nrow(future_ssps) * length(example_wsd))
idx <- 1L

invisible(
  capture.output(
    suppressWarnings(
      suppressMessages({
        for (wsd in example_wsd) {
          pk <- quartile_parks$park_unit[quartile_parks$wsd_source_id == wsd]

          for (i in seq_len(nrow(future_ssps))) {
            s <- future_ssps[i, ]

            spei_ts_list[[idx]] <- run_spei_for_park(
              wsd,
              pk,
              s$model,
              s$ssp,
              s$run
            )

            idx <- idx + 1L
          }
        }
      })
    ),
    file = nullfile()
  )
)

spei_ts <- rbindlist(spei_ts_list, use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE)

# Ensemble summary per park × month
spei_summary <- spei_ts %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  left_join(quartile_parks %>% select(park_unit, raw_spei_change_p50), by = "park_unit") %>%
  mutate(
    park_label = glue("{park_unit}  (median Δ SPEI = {round(raw_spei_change_p50, 3)})"),
    year_dec = as.numeric(format(ym, "%Y")) +
      (as.numeric(format(ym, "%m")) - 1) / 12
  ) %>%
  group_by(park_unit, park_label, raw_spei_change_p50, ym, year_dec, period) %>%
  summarise(
    spei_mean = mean(spei, na.rm = TRUE),
    spei_p10  = quantile(spei, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
    spei_p90  = quantile(spei, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(park_label = fct_reorder(park_label, -raw_spei_change_p50, .fun = function(x) x[1]))
```

## Figure 1 — SPEI-12 time series (historical + future)

Ensemble-mean SPEI-12 with 10th–90th percentile ribbon across all GCM × SSP runs. The
vertical dashed line marks the boundary between the calibration period and the future
projection window.

```{r fig-spei-timeseries, fig.height=9}
drought_bands <- tibble(
  ymin  = c(-Inf, -2.0, -1.5, -1.0),
  ymax  = c(-2.0, -1.5, -1.0, 0.0),
  label = c("Extreme", "Severe", "Moderate", "Mild"),
  fill  = c(col_extreme, col_severe, col_moderate, "#FEF3C7")
)

spei_summary %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year_dec)) +
  geom_rect(
    data = drought_bands,
    aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.08
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = setNames(drought_bands$fill, drought_bands$label),
    name = "Drought class",
    guide = guide_legend(order = 2)
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = fut_start - 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = col_neutral, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = col_neutral, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = spei_p10, ymax = spei_p90, group = period), fill = col_highlight, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_point(aes(y = spei_mean, color = period, group = period), linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("historical" = col_hist, "future" = col_future),
    labels = c("historical" = glue("Historical ({hist_start}–{hist_end})"),
               "future" = glue("Future ({fut_start}–{fut_end})")),
    name = NULL,
    guide = guide_legend(order = 1)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~park_label, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1975, 2075, 10), labels = seq(1975, 2075, 10)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-spei_inf_cap, 2.5)) +
  labs(
    title = "SPEI-12 Time Series — Historical and Projected",
    subtitle = "Ribbon = 10th–90th percentile across GCM ensemble. Infinite SPEI values are capped for plotting and means.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "SPEI-12"
  ) +
  theme_rapid() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"))
```



## Figure 2 — Δ SPEI by SSP scenario

Do higher-emission scenarios project meaningfully more drying?

```{r fig-by-ssp, fig.height=7}
delta_spei_ensemble <- spei_ts %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  group_by(wsd_source_id, park_unit, model, ssp, run, period) %>%
  summarise(mean_spei = mean(spei, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = mean_spei) %>%
  filter(!is.na(historical), !is.na(future)) %>%
  mutate(delta_spei = future - historical) %>%
  left_join(
    quartile_parks %>% select(park_unit, raw_spei_change_p50),
    by = "park_unit"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    park_label = glue("{park_unit}  (median Δ SPEI = {round(raw_spei_change_p50, 3)})"),
    park_label = fct_reorder(park_label, -raw_spei_change_p50, .fun = function(x) x[1])
  )

delta_spei_ensemble %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = ssp, y = delta_spei, fill = ssp)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = col_neutral, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.75, outlier.shape = 21, outlier.size = 1.5, outlier.fill = "white", width = 0.55) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point", shape = 23, size = 3, fill = "white", color = col_highlight) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = "SSP") +
  facet_wrap(~ park_label, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Δ SPEI by Emissions Scenario",
    subtitle = "Diamond = median across models within each SSP. Dashed line = no change.",
    x = "Scenario (SSP)",
    y = "Δ SPEI-12 (future − historical)"
  ) +
  theme_rapid()
```

## Figure 6 — P50 Δ SPEI compared against drought thresholds

If a park's current mean SPEI sits near 0 (near-normal) but Δ SPEI is −1, the future mean
would fall near the moderate drought threshold. This plot contextualises the *change* against
SPEI classification thresholds assuming a historical baseline mean of 0.

```{r fig-threshold-context, fig.height=5}
exposure %>%
  group_by(park_unit) %>%
  summarise(p50 = mean(raw_spei_change_p50, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(future_spei_class = cut(p50, breaks = spei_breaks, labels = spei_labels, right = TRUE)) %>%
  count(future_spei_class) %>%
  filter(!is.na(future_spei_class)) %>%
  mutate(future_spei_class = fct_relevel(future_spei_class, spei_labels)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = future_spei_class, y = n, fill = future_spei_class)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5, color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(spei_colours, spei_labels)) +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 35)) +
  labs(
    title = "Projected Future SPEI Class (Assuming Historical Baseline ≈ 0)",
    subtitle = "Bars show number of parks whose median Δ SPEI would place them in each SPEI category.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of park units"
  ) +
  theme_rapid()
```

```{r fig-top-bottom, fig.height=9}
make_ranked_plot <- function(df, title_str, dot_col) {
  df %>%
    mutate(park_unit = fct_reorder(park_unit, mean_p50)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = park_unit)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = col_neutral) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -1, linetype = "dotted", color = col_dry, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = mean_p10, ymax = mean_p90), color = "grey65", linewidth = 0.8) +

    ) +

}
```

```{r, results = "hide"}

 inner_join(exposure, by = c("wsd_source_id", "park_unit"))
```

```{r}
make_continuous_pal <- function(vals) {
  vals <- vals[is.finite(vals)]   # drop NA / NaN / Inf before range calc

  if (!length(vals)) stop("No finite values in column.")

  mn <- min(vals)
  mx <- max(vals)

  # Guard against zero-width domain
  if (mn == mx) mn <- mx - 1e-6

  if (mn >= 0) {
    colorNumeric(c("lightgreen", "darkgreen"), domain = c(mn, mx),
                 na.color = "transparent")
  } else if (mx <= 0) {
    colorNumeric(c("darkred", "orange"), domain = c(mn, mx),
                 na.color = "transparent")
  } else {
    n      <- 512
    neg_n  <- round(n * abs(mn) / (abs(mn) + mx))
    pos_n  <- n - neg_n
    colors <- c(
      colorRampPalette(c("darkred", "orange"))(neg_n),
      colorRampPalette(c("lightgreen", "darkgreen"))(pos_n)
    )
    colorNumeric(colors, domain = c(mn, mx), na.color = "transparent")
  }
}

render_map <- function(data, col, title) {
  pal    <- make_continuous_pal(data[[col]])
  coords <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(data, 4326))

  leaflet(data) %>%
    addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") %>%
    addCircleMarkers(
      lng         = coords[, 1],
      lat         = coords[, 2],
      radius      = 5,
      fillColor   = ~ pal(get(col)),
      fillOpacity = 0.85,
      color       = "white",
      weight      = 0.5,
      popup       = ~ paste0(
        "<b>", wsd_source_id, "</b><br>",
        park_name, "<br>",
        water_system_name, "<br>",
        title, ": <b>", round(get(col), 3), "</b>"
      )
    ) %>%
    addLegend(
      position  = "bottomright",
      pal       = pal,
      values    = data[[col]],
      title     = title,
      labFormat = labelFormat(digits = 2)
    )
}

maps <- list(
  render_map(water_supplies, "raw_spei_change_p10", "Δ SPEI-12 (P10)"),
  render_map(water_supplies, "raw_spei_change_p50", "Δ SPEI-12 (P50)"),
  render_map(water_supplies, "raw_spei_change_p90", "Δ SPEI-12 (P90)")
)

htmltools::tagList(maps)
```

# Climatic Water Balance — Seasonal Breakdown

Understanding *when* the water deficit is projected to change helps translate the annual
SPEI signal into operational planning. Here we look at projected changes in the raw
monthly P − PET balance.

```{r fig-seasonal-balance, fig.height=8}
climate_monthly %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  filter(wsd_source_id %in% example_wsd) %>%
  filter(drought_period %in% c("historical", "future")) %>%
  mutate(period = recode(drought_period, historical = "Historical", future = "Future")) %>%
  filter(input_window == "reporting" | reporting_period %in% TRUE) %>%
  left_join(quartile_parks %>% select(park_unit, raw_spei_change_p50), by = "park_unit") %>%
  mutate(
    park_label = glue("{park_unit}  (Δ SPEI P50 = {round(raw_spei_change_p50, 3)})"),
    month_name = factor(month.abb[month], levels = month.abb)
  ) %>%
  group_by(park_unit, park_label, month_name, period) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_balance = mean(monthly_balance, na.rm = TRUE),
    p10_balance = quantile(monthly_balance, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
    p90_balance = quantile(monthly_balance, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = month_name, group = period)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10_balance, ymax = p90_balance, fill = period), alpha = 0.20) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_balance, color = period), linewidth = 1.0) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = col_neutral, linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Historical" = col_hist, "Future" = col_future), name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Historical" = col_hist, "Future" = col_future), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) +
  facet_wrap(~ park_label, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Climatic Water Balance (Precipitation − PET)",
    subtitle = "Ribbon = P10–P90 across GCM ensemble. Below zero = evaporative demand exceeds supply.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "P − PET (mm/month)"
  ) +
  theme_rapid() +
  theme(legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"))
```

# Interpretation Guide

| Δ SPEI (P50) | Model agreement (% drying) | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| < −0.5 | > 70% | **High-confidence severe drying.** Strong consistent signal across models; major drought exposure risk. |
| −0.5 to −0.2 | > 60% | **Moderate drying.** Meaningful but not extreme shift; monitor storage and reliability. |
| −0.2 to 0.0 | Mixed | **Slight drying tendency.** Signal present but within noise range; low near-term concern. |
| ~0.0 | Mixed | **Stable.** No meaningful projected change in drought conditions. |
| > 0.0 | < 40% | **Wetting tendency.** Supply conditions projected to improve on average; verify with P90 for stress-testing. |

> **P10 as a stress-test:** For long-term infrastructure decisions, `raw_spei_change_p10`
> represents the pessimistic end of the model envelope — use it to design for a plausible
> worst-case scenario even where the median signal is modest.
>
> **Future `-Inf` diagnostics:** `raw_spei_future_report_pct_neg_inf_months` records the
> percentage of future reporting months where SPEI was unboundedly dry before capping.
> Higher values suggest stronger or less stable drying signals and should be reviewed alongside
> the main Δ SPEI metrics.
>
> **Scale sensitivity:** SPEI-12 captures multi-season hydrological drought. Parks relying on
> small, flashy catchments may be better characterised with SPEI-3 or SPEI-6.
